findings.text: Gap search within a caller window reports success only when a hole large enough for the requested size exists, and on success sets the cursor lower bound and upper bound to the chosen hole with length matching the request. The forward helper prefers the lowest fitting hole while the reverse helper prefers the highest fitting hole. When no hole fits, the result is a busy condition, including cases where the request fits a hole but not the window ends. When the window itself is smaller than the request the result is an invalid condition. Coverage includes small fixed intervals with an interior hole, large power of two sizes, full exhaustion, and gaps inside deep trees.

Cyclic allocation hands out consecutive locations starting at the range minimum and advances a caller next cursor in lockstep, so each allocation is predictable from the iteration count. The tree level helper stores a value equal to the tree pointer at the allocated location. Erased locations inside a nearly full bounded interval are reused on subsequent calls, with the next cursor set just past the reused slot. After exhausting the full address space the operation reports failure with a nonzero status.

Bulk population of many adjacent fixed stride intervals followed by clearing of a middle interval exercises minimum spanning behavior of branch nodes. A separate non kernel allocation identity is installed around such stress sequences and cleared afterwards, indicating that test allocations can be attributed to a synthetic owner.

Cursor status distinguishes start, paused, none, root, active, overflow and underflow. With only a root entry, walk and directional scan and find operations move among start, root and none with bounds covering either the singleton or the surrounding empty space. With multiple stored intervals, the same operations move among start, paused, active, overflow and underflow, where active means positioned on an entry or gap inside the tree, overflow means past the search maximum, and underflow means before the search minimum. Pause preserves position for resume, widening the limit can return from overflow or underflow to active, and spanning a limit without crossing data stays active.

The observable cursor state comprises a lower bound, an upper bound, a status, an offset, and an association with one tree. Lower and upper bounds delimit the current entry or gap after each walk, scan, find or gap search. Status records the state machine outcome described separately. Offset selects a slot inside the current node and is explicitly cleared in some none to active transitions.

Mutating cursor sequences acquire the cursor exclusive lock before positioning and storing and release it afterwards, with cursor destruction occurring after release. Read only gap searches execute inside a read side critical section bracketed by acquire and release. One cyclic allocation batch holds the tree lock across many cursor allocations, while other allocation loops use per operation tree helpers without an outer held lock in the fragment.

Each routine under study is a boot time self test helper taking a tree pointer and returning no value. Together they cover branch node spanning, forward and reverse gap search windows, gap fill and exhaustion, exhaustive cursor status transitions for root only and multi interval trees, and cyclic allocation including wrap and overflow.

Every expectation is enforced by a bug check macro that aborts the boot test on mismatch, so any deviation in returned status, entry value, bounds, or cursor status is fatal rather than recoverable. Tests toggle a synthetic non kernel allocation identity around large loops and must restore the normal identity afterwards.
